instruction: Add a new sheet called "Analysis" and merge cells B1:D1 to enter the title "Financial Overview". Below that, merge cells B2:C2 for "Principal Amounts" and merge cells D2:E2 for "Interest Details".

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new sheet named 'Analysis' with merged cells and specific text. The evaluator verifies: (1) Sheet 'Analysis' exists, (2) B1:D1 merged with 'Financial Overview', (3) B2:C2 merged with 'Principal Amounts', (4) D2:E2 merged with 'Interest Details', (5) Adjacent cells are not merged.

llm_judge_reasons: Merge detection logic is flawed: Line 54 checks if a cell is part of ANY merged range, but doesn't verify cells are merged in the CORRECT range (e.g., B1, C1, D1 should all be part of B1:D1, not separate merges)
The function could pass even if B1:B2 and C1:D1 were merged instead of B1:D1, because it only checks individual cell merge status without verifying the actual merge range boundaries

Scoring logic is inconsistent: cells with value checks get 0.5 for merge + 0.5 for value, but cells without value checks get 0.5 for merge + 0.5 bonus (line 64-65), making different checks worth different amounts
The evaluator doesn't verify that the merged ranges are exactly B1:D1, B2:C2, and D2:E2 as specified in the instruction - it only checks if individual cells are merged
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace the merge detection with actual merge range verification: check if ws.merged_cells contains the exact ranges 'B1:D1', 'B2:C2', and 'D2:E2'
Use openpyxl's merged_cells.ranges to get all merged ranges and verify the expected ranges exist
Fix scoring logic: make each check worth equal weight (1.0 / total_checks) and remove the inconsistent bonus scoring
For cells that are part of a merge range, verify they belong to the expected merge range, not just any merge range
